fields.h1: Build a Training Acknowledgment Form Signed at Each Session
fields.hero_description: Build a training acknowledgment form that saves who was trained, by whom, and when, in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Every Signed Training Record Holds
fields.features_subheading: A signature alone proves little. These six pieces turn a training acknowledgment form into a record you can look up later.
fields.feature_1:
Course, trainer, and date on every signature

The app saves each signature with the course name, the trainer, the date, and the site. Six months later, a supervisor can see who taught that session and where it took place.
fields.feature_2:
The statement each trainee agrees to

Write the acknowledgment in your own words, such as attending the full session and understanding the material. The wording a trainee saw is kept beside the signature.
fields.feature_3:
Signatures captured on a phone or tablet

Trainees type their name and draw a signature with a finger. A crew can pass one tablet around after a talk, and a remote employee can sign from a link on their phone.
fields.feature_4:
A list of who still has to sign

Assign a training to a group, and a screen shows who signed and who has not. The app emails a reminder to anyone missing a signature, and the list updates as each one comes in.
fields.feature_5:
Each person's training history in one place

Each acknowledgment is a row in a database you own. Open one person to see every course they signed, or filter by course to see everyone who completed it this calendar year.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can move to your own servers

Export the full codebase to your GitHub repository on paid plans when training records need to sit beside an HR system you already run. Host it anywhere and keep building.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Trainings That End in a Signature
fields.tab_content_1:
9 roofers sign one tablet before anyone climbs

Dario Mendhall gives the talk at the Elm Street job before the crew goes up: 15 minutes on setting and tying off ladders. Then he passes his tablet down the line. All 9 roofers at Halvorsen Roofing sign under the same topic and trainer, and the record reaches the office before the first shingle comes off.
fields.tab_content_2:
One wrong answer, and it is back to the video

Quillfeather Software assigns a 25-minute phishing awareness video to 64 staff. The signature box appears only after 3 check questions on what they watched, and a wrong answer sends that person back to the video. By the deadline, 59 of 64 have signed, and the 5 still rewatching sit on the security lead's list.
fields.tab_content_3:
Abel co-signs when Wynn takes the slicer apart

New cooks at Saltgrass Kitchen stay off the meat slicer until two people sign. Chef Abel Strand walks Wynn Cardoza through the blade guard and cleaning, and Wynn signs that he was trained. Abel co-signs only after watching Wynn take the slicer apart and clean it himself. The record shows Wynn cleared on March 12.
fields.tab_content_4:
Who is due within 30 days, by name

Ostrander Property Group repeats fire extinguisher training every 12 months, and each signed acknowledgment sets a technician's next due date. Facilities manager Marguerite Osei opens a dashboard showing 4 of 22 technicians due within 30 days and emails each of the 4 a reminder from that list.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Training Acknowledgment
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a training acknowledgment form that ties each signature to its course and trainer, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the trainings people sign for
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the statement in plain words
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Record the session, not only the name
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Decide who signs and in what order
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the trainings people already sign for on paper, such as safety talks, video courses, and equipment sign-offs. Each one becomes a type on the form, because a crew talk and a solo online course collect signatures in different ways.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write the sentence the trainee signs under. Say what they confirm, such as attending the whole session and understanding it, and name a person to ask with questions. Keep it short enough to read on a phone before signing.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add fields for the course name, who taught it, when it ran, and where. A signature with no course attached tells nobody what was covered when a supervisor looks it up months later. Make the course a required field.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose whether the trainee signs alone or a trainer co-signs after watching the skill. For group talks, let one tablet collect a signature from each attendee in turn under the same session details. Nobody retypes the topic for each person.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the training types, the statement, and the signing order into one prompt. Emergent builds the training acknowledgment form, the database behind it, and a screen showing who has signed. Change any question later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_des: For training you repeat, set the interval your own policy uses, such as once a year. The app sets a next due date from each signature and emails a reminder to anyone coming due within the window you choose.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sign a test record as a trainee on your phone, then co-sign it as the trainer. Check that the record lands in the table with the course and the date, and that the next due date is right.

faq_plan.q: What is a training acknowledgment form?
faq_plan.a: A training acknowledgment form is a signed record that an employee attended a training and understood it. Lumin describes it as a document used by employers to verify that an employee has attended and understood a required training session. Above the signature line, name the session it covers and who led it.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a training acknowledgment form?
faq_plan.a: List the trainings that need a signature, write the statement each trainee signs, and decide whether a trainer co-signs. Put those decisions into one prompt for Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the form, a table of every signature, and a view of the signatures still missing. To change a question later, describe the change in a new prompt.

faq_plan.q: What should the statement on a training acknowledgment form say?
faq_plan.a: It should say what the trainee confirms, in one or two plain sentences. On a City of Little Rock form, the signer confirms they watched the training class listed above in its entirety. Add that they understood the material and know whom to ask with questions, then put the signature and the date under it.

faq_plan.q: When should employees sign a training acknowledgment form?
faq_plan.a: Right after the training ends, while the trainee is still in the room or on the course page. A sign-off collected a week later is easy to forget and hard to chase. The step before training is a separate record: an employee asks for a course on a training request form, and the acknowledgment closes it out once they finish.

faq_plan.q: Should a trainer sign the training acknowledgment form too?
faq_plan.a: For hands-on skills, yes. A trainer's co-signature shows that someone watched the trainee do the task, not only that they sat through the session. Have the trainee sign first and the trainer second. Emergent can build the form to keep each record open until both signatures are in.

faq_plan.q: Does a training acknowledgment form work on a phone?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Trainees sign with a finger on the screen, or open a link at the end of an online course and sign there. A form built with Emergent captures the signature and saves it with the session details in a database you own, with no response caps.

faq_plan.q: What is a safety training acknowledgment form?
faq_plan.a: It is a training acknowledgment for a safety session, such as a ladder talk or a fire extinguisher class. On one published safety version, the signer writes: I acknowledge that I have attended this training session. It is a different record from an employee handbook acknowledgment form, which covers the handbook itself, not a session someone attended.

faq_plan.q: Can one training acknowledgment form cover several trainings?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a training type field and show different questions for each type, such as check questions after a video course or a co-signature for equipment. Every signature still lands as its own record, and you can filter by course later. Emergent builds that logic from a plain-English prompt.

faq_plan.q: What fields go on a training acknowledgment form?
faq_plan.a: Start with the trainee's name and job title, then the course title, who ran it, when, and where. The Mitti template, for one, records the date, the trainer, the branch, and the type of training. Close with the acknowledgment statement, the signature, and the date signed.

faq_plan.q: Should a training acknowledgment form ask for feedback on the course?
faq_plan.a: No. Keep the acknowledgment short: what was covered, then the signature. Ask what people thought of the trainer and the content on a separate training feedback form, where they can answer honestly without their opinion sitting next to their signature.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is signature sheets: a city PDF where staff confirm they watched a class in its entirety, a college and a back-office PDF, Lumin, Mitti and Jotform templates, a Westlaw standard form and a Texas agency volunteer form. Each one stops at a name, a date and a signature line on paper. This page builds the acknowledgment as a training record: a crew signing a toolbox talk on one tablet at the job site, an online course with check questions before the signature, an equipment sign-off that the trainer co-signs, and refresher dates that come due on a dashboard, then answers what the form is, what the statement says and who signs it.
